findings.title: Redis OSS 5.0.5 replication group is in Extended Support (paying since 2026-02-01)
findings.description:
aws_elasticache_replication_group.kong (redis.tf:1) uses engine redis (redis.tf:7) with engine_version = var.redis_engine_version, default "5.0.5" (variables.tf:487), and parameter group family var.redis_family = "redis5.0" (variables.tf:494). Redis OSS 5 standard support ended 2026-01-31; Extended Support Year 1 charges apply since 2026-02-01, the next price step is 2027-02-01, and AWS upgrades remaining Redis OSS 5 caches to the latest Valkey after 2029-01-31 (source: AWS docs, live data unavailable). The cache exists only when var.enable_redis = true (default false), so whether it is deployed is unknown. Risk score 6 (High): version < 5.0.6 (+2), automatic failover / Multi-AZ off (+2), Kong 2.8.1 Redis client older than 3 years (+1), no staging environment found (+1). Recommended: Valkey 7.2 (rule 2) to keep an in-place rollback to Redis OSS 7.1, then a newer Valkey. Blocker: transit_encryption_enabled is not set. Estimated Extended Support exposure ~$40/month (estimate, 2 x cache.t2.small). Moving to Redis OSS 6 is not recommended: it only postpones charges until 2027-02-01.

findings.title: In-transit encryption is not enabled; a Valkey target needs it
findings.description: transit_encryption_enabled is not set on aws_elasticache_replication_group.kong, so in-transit encryption is off. The CloudFormation docs require TransitEncryptionEnabled when creating a Valkey replication group; whether an in-place engine change also requires it is not confirmed. Enabling TLS changes how every Kong node connects to Redis, so it is not set automatically. Proposed manual change: enable TLS (transit_encryption_mode = "preferred" first, then "required") and switch Kong's Redis plugin configuration to TLS, or choose Redis OSS 7.1 (target C), which does not need this change.

findings.title: Kong rate-limiting counters stored in Redis
findings.description: The cache backs Kong rate-limiting counters and caching. No Lua scripting (EVAL/EVALSHA/SCRIPT LOAD/FCALL) or redis_version parsing was found in this repository; the Kong plugin code is outside it. Counters survive the upgrade. Kong loses the connection during failover (30-60 s write pause from 5.0.5). Test rate limiting against a Valkey dev cache and confirm Kong's Redis timeout and fault-tolerance settings.

findings.title: Endpoint published by DNS name through SSM
findings.description: The primary endpoint address is written to SSM parameter /<service>/<environment>/redis/primary-endpoint and is read by consumers (commented example at cloud-init.sh:196). No hard-coded node IPs next to port 6379 were found. The endpoint DNS name stays the same after the upgrade; no change needed.

findings.title: Custom parameter group on family redis5.0 with no custom parameters
findings.description: aws_elasticache_parameter_group.kong uses family var.redis_family = "redis5.0" (variables.tf:494) and defines no parameter blocks, so it carries default values only. The remediation must create a group in the target family (valkey7 for Valkey 7.2, valkey8, valkey9 or redis7) because the family cannot change in place; no static values need copying.

findings.title: Cache is optional (enable_redis defaults to false); deployment state unknown
findings.description: The replication group is created only when var.enable_redis is true (default false, variables.tf:473). No tfvars or caller configuration is in this repository and live access was off, so it is unknown whether any deployment of this module has the cache. Callers may also override redis_engine_version, redis_family, redis_instance_type and redis_instance_count.

findings.title: Live data, AWS Health and Trusted Advisor not used
findings.description: live_access=off was set in the plan context. No caller identity, AWS Health events, Trusted Advisor findings, live caches, or DescribeCacheEngineVersions results were read. Status comes from the AWS documentation lifecycle table, drift was not checked, and target versions (7.2, 8.2, 9.1) are not confirmed for the Region. live_data=unavailable in every plan block.

findings.title: AWS provider version is not pinned; CI uses Terraform 0.12.13
findings.description: The repository has no required_providers block or .terraform.lock.hcl, so the AWS provider version is chosen by the caller. engine = "valkey" on aws_elasticache_replication_group needs a recent AWS provider 5.x, which does not support Terraform 0.12. CI (fmt/init only, no apply) pins Terraform 0.12.13. Confirm the caller's Terraform and provider versions before the remediation; if they are on provider 4.x or Terraform 0.12, upgrading them first is a separate major-version change (potential blocker).
